title: Bounded finite free complexes over stalks have minimal homotopy representatives
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $y\in Y$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, and $t:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)\to S$ the morphism induced by the residue quotient. Let $P$ be a cochain complex of $\mathcal O_S$-modules [def-pc-derived-category], supported in degrees $0$ through $d\in\mathbb N$, whose every term is isomorphic to a finite free sheaf [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Then there is a cochain complex $Q$ on $S$, supported in the same interval and with finite free terms, together with a homotopy equivalence $P\simeq Q$, such that every differential of the termwise pullback $t^*Q$ [def-pc-derived-pullback] is zero. A homotopy equivalence consists of two chain maps whose composites are chain homotopic to the respective identities. There is no hypothesis on residue cohomology and no claim that $Q$ is supported at one degree.

source.place: Tag 00MT, lemma-add-trivial-complex, iterated unit-entry cancellation; blueprint lem-pc-perfect-locus, proof step 4

proof.text: Choose a finite free rank n(j) for each term. Strongly induct on the natural number sum of n(k) for k in {0,...,d}. If all residue differentials vanish, return P and HomotopyEquiv.refl P with its original support and freeness.

Otherwise apply [lem-pc-finite-free-stalk-unit-cancellation]. It returns a homotopy equivalent complement P' with chosen ranks n', an index i<d, n'(i)+1=n(i), n'(i+1)+1=n(i+1), and unchanged ranks elsewhere. A case split at i and i+1 gives n'(k)<=n(k) for every k. Since i belongs to {0,...,d} and n'(i)<n(i), Finset.sum_lt_sum proves that the complement has strictly smaller rank sum.

Apply the strong induction hypothesis to the complement, using its support bounds and free identifications. Compose the cancellation homotopy equivalence with the inductively obtained one by HomotopyEquiv.trans. The resulting complex has the required bounds, finite free terms and zero residue differentials. The zero-rank case needs no separate construction, since no cancellation can have rank sum less than zero.

proof_origin.place: Tag 00MT; strong rank-sum induction formalized in Lean, one sheaf cancellation separated into its own node

lean.statement:
theorem exists_stalk_minimal_complex {Y : Scheme.{u}} (y : Y)
    (P : CochainComplex (Spec (Y.presheaf.stalk y)).Modules ℤ) (d : ℕ)
    (hge : P.IsStrictlyGE 0) (hle : P.IsStrictlyLE d)
    (hfree : ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ s : ℕ, Nonempty
      (P.X n ≅ SheafOfModules.free
        (R := (Spec (Y.presheaf.stalk y)).ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin s)))) :
    ∃ Q : CochainComplex (Spec (Y.presheaf.stalk y)).Modules ℤ,
      Nonempty (HomotopyEquiv P Q) ∧ Q.IsStrictlyGE 0 ∧ Q.IsStrictlyLE d ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ s : ℕ, Nonempty
        (Q.X n ≅ SheafOfModules.free
          (R := (Spec (Y.presheaf.stalk y)).ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin s)))) ∧
      ∀ a b : ℤ,
        (((Modules.pullback (Spec.map (Y.residue y))).mapHomologicalComplex _).obj
          Q).d a b = 0
